definition: To move hurriedly with short quick steps
etymology: Possibly from hurry-scurry, a reduplication of 'hurry'
contextSentence: They would scurry around and I would hope that none of them would stay around.
contextSentenceKo: 그것들이 종종걸음으로 돌아다니면 나는 아무것도 주변에 남지 않기를 바랐습니다.

definition: Routine tasks, especially household ones
etymology: From Middle English 'chare' meaning 'a turn of work'
contextSentence: Do your chores and don't come back until they're done.
contextSentenceKo: 집안일 하고 다 끝날 때까지 돌아오지 마.

definition: Providing encouragement or emotional help
contextSentence: It was kind of the beginning of me realizing that I wasn't in a supportive environment.
contextSentenceKo: 그때부터 제가 지지적인 환경에 있지 않다는 것을 깨닫기 시작했습니다.

definition: In every case or on every occasion; always
contextSentence: I'd call him out to look at the task being done and invariably it was never good enough.
contextSentenceKo: 아버지를 불러서 끝낸 일을 보여드리면, 어김없이 충분하지 않았습니다.

definition: To strengthen one's commitment to a particular strategy or course of action
etymology: Originally from blackjack: doubling your bet after seeing initial cards
contextSentence: So I doubled down on that and I worked hard.
contextSentenceKo: 그래서 저는 거기에 더욱 매진했고 열심히 일했습니다.

definition: Comfort or consolation in a time of distress or sadness
contextSentence: The only solace I had was to work hard.
contextSentenceKo: 제가 가진 유일한 위안은 열심히 일하는 것이었습니다.

definition: The activity or occupation of making or repairing things in wood
etymology: From Anglo-Norman French 'carpenterie', from Latin 'carpentarius' (wagon maker)
contextSentence: I drove a taxi, I did carpentry, I cut lawns, I washed windows.
contextSentenceKo: 택시를 몰고, 목공 일을 하고, 잔디를 깎고, 유리창을 닦았습니다.

definition: Expelled from a property, typically with the support of the law
etymology: From Latin 'evictus', past participle of 'evincere' (to conquer)
contextSentence: I got evicted from my apartment and I went back in with my mom at the age of 30.
contextSentenceKo: 아파트에서 쫓겨나서 서른 살에 다시 어머니 집으로 들어갔습니다.

definition: An experienced and trusted adviser
etymology: From Greek 'Mentor', the adviser of the young Telemachus in Homer's Odyssey
contextSentence: That's when I met my first mentor that transformed my life.
contextSentenceKo: 그때 제 인생을 변화시킨 첫 번째 멘토를 만났습니다.

definition: The principle that hard work is intrinsically virtuous or worthy of reward
contextSentence: Because you really have a great work ethic.
contextSentenceKo: 왜냐하면 당신은 정말 훌륭한 직업 윤리를 가지고 있으니까요.

definition: The aspect of someone's character that is presented to or perceived by others
meaningKo: 페르소나, 외적 인격, 겉으로 보이는 모습
contextSentence: You take on those labels and you wear them like they're your persona.
contextSentenceKo: 그런 꼬리표를 받아들이고 마치 자신의 페르소나처럼 걸치고 다니게 됩니다.

definition: The human soul, mind, or spirit
contextSentence: The most powerful force in the human psyche is how we describe ourselves to ourself.
contextSentenceKo: 인간의 정신에서 가장 강력한 힘은 스스로를 어떻게 묘사하느냐입니다.

definition: To program again or differently
contextSentence: We're gonna reprogram your brain. Your brain is like software, we're just gonna reprogram it.
contextSentenceKo: 당신의 뇌를 재프로그래밍할 겁니다. 뇌는 소프트웨어와 같아서, 그냥 다시 프로그래밍하면 됩니다.

definition: Having the ability to find quick and clever ways to overcome difficulties
contextSentence: I became resourceful. I became capable of doing things I didn't know I was gonna do.
contextSentenceKo: 저는 수완이 좋아졌습니다. 할 수 있을 줄 몰랐던 일들을 할 수 있게 되었죠.

definition: Shy and reticent; characterized by interest in one's own mental life
contextSentence: You're quiet, you're introverted, and you take on those labels.
contextSentenceKo: 넌 조용하고, 내성적이야, 그리고 그런 꼬리표를 받아들이게 됩니다.

definition: In a strong, rough, and attractive manner
contextSentence: Loser out, ruggedly handsome in.
contextSentenceKo: 루저는 빼고, 거칠면서도 잘생긴 모습을 넣는 거죠.

definition: As a result of a sudden inner impulse without premeditation
etymology: From Latin 'spontaneus' (of one's own free will)
contextSentence: Then spontaneously one morning I was in the shower and I said I'm the greatest real estate agent in my area.
contextSentenceKo: 그러다 어느 날 아침 샤워를 하던 중 자발적으로 '나는 이 지역 최고의 부동산 중개인이다'라고 말했습니다.

definition: The lowest load-bearing part of a building; an underlying basis or principle
etymology: From Latin 'fundatio' from 'fundare' (to lay the bottom)
contextSentence: When you're down there and you think there's nothing left, it's the foundation to grow from.
contextSentenceKo: 바닥까지 내려가서 아무것도 남지 않았다고 생각할 때, 그것이 바로 성장의 토대입니다.

definition: Made a thorough or dramatic change in form, appearance, or character
contextSentence: That's when I met my first mentor that transformed my life.
contextSentenceKo: 그때 제 인생을 변화시킨 첫 번째 멘토를 만났습니다.

definition: To define again or differently
etymology: re- (again) + define (from Latin 'definire' = to set bounds)
contextSentence: Today is the first day of the rest of your life and you get to redefine yourself.
contextSentenceKo: 오늘은 남은 인생의 첫날이며, 당신은 자신을 재정의할 수 있습니다.

definition: Becoming or making smaller in size or amount
etymology: From Old English 'scrincan' (to shrivel, dry up)
contextSentence: He looked at me and I felt myself shrinking down.
contextSentenceKo: 그가 나를 쳐다봤고 나는 스스로 위축되는 느낌이었습니다.

definition: A person greatly admired, loved, or revered
contextSentence: Who's an idol that you have?
contextSentenceKo: 당신의 우상은 누구인가요?

definition: The lowest possible level
contextSentence: I don't know if it broke my spirit or if I thought I'd hit rock bottom.
contextSentenceKo: 그것이 제 정신을 무너뜨린 건지, 바닥을 쳤다고 느낀 건지 모르겠습니다.

definition: To throw (something) forcefully in a specified direction; to cause (light or shadow) to appear on a surface
contextSentence: This shadow cast over me and he goes, do you have any idea what it takes to put food on the table?
contextSentenceKo: 그림자가 저를 덮쳤고 그가 말했습니다, 밥벌이가 얼마나 힘든지 알기나 하냐?
